(2021)—along with broader PFDM literature—misinterprets the underlying physics by treating the background as a single dark matter fluid. They point out that the metric was originally derived for a dual-component system consisting of pressureless cold dark matter (WIMPs) coexisting with an inhomogeneous phantom scalar field (an exotic dark energy candidate with equation of state $w < -1$). By reviewing the exact analytic solutions and stress-energy tensor conditions of their original model, the authors show that the logarithmic metric represents an extreme, localized mathematical limit rather than a realistic galactic halo, warning against applying it blindly to extreme astrophysical scenarios.

papers.title: AllBRICQS: the All-sky BRIght, Complete Quasar Survey - Quasar Selection and Final Southern $G_{\rm RP}<16$ Sample
papers.authors: Christian Wolf, Christopher A. Onken, Wei Jeat Hon, Samuel Lai, Patrick Tisserand, Rachel Webster
papers.abstract: We describe the final quasar sample from the Southern part of the All-sky BRIght, Complete Quasar Survey (AllBRICQS), which aimed to discover the remaining optically bright quasars using data from Gaia and WISE. We discuss our final selection and present a further 119 quasars in the redshift range $z=[0.03;4.35]$. This brings the sample of spectroscopically confirmed quasars with $G_{\rm RP}<16$ and $z>0.1$ at Dec$<+20^{\circ}$ and Galactic latitude $|b|>10^{\circ}$ to 745 objects. The spectra from the ANU 2.3m telescope at Siding Spring Observatory cover a wavelength range from 360 to 950 nm with $R\sim3000$. For redshifts of $z>0.12$, we expect the sample to be complete at $G_{\rm RP}<16$, a regime that is usually avoided by large spectroscopic surveys due to detector saturation. We note that at least one strongly lensed quasar has escaped our selection.

conclusions: Spectroscopic follow-up at the ANU 2.3m telescope confirmed 119 new bright quasars ($z \in [0.03, 4.35]$), bringing the total AllBRICQS Southern discoveries to 270 and the complete Southern sample ($z > 0.1$, $G_{\rm RP} < 16$, $\text{Dec} < +20^\circ$, $|b| > 10^\circ$) to 745 confirmed quasars with a median redshift of $z \sim 0.5$.

In the bright regime ($G_{\rm RP} < 16$), combining Gaia astrometric filtering with a simple linear cut in $(G_{\rm RP} - \text{W1})_0$ vs. $\text{W1} - \text{W2}$ colour space cleanly isolates quasars from Galactic stars without needing machine learning or Bayesian classifiers, achieving near-total completeness for $z > 0.12$.

The primary sources of selection incompleteness are low-redshift ($z < 0.125$) Seyfert-1 galaxies whose host galaxy starlight dilutes the nuclear infrared excess, and sub-arcsecond extended systems (such as strongly gravitationally lensed quasars, dual AGN, or quasars with optical jets) that fail Gaia's astrometric point-source cuts.
ai.summary: Quasars—extremely luminous active galactic nuclei powered by matter accreting onto supermassive black holes—serve as valuable cosmic beacons, yet many of the brightest ones in the Southern sky have gone unidentified because they saturate the detectors of large modern spectroscopic surveys (which typically only observe fainter than magnitude $\sim 16$) and blend in with Milky Way stars. To complete the census of the brightest Southern quasars, the authors conclude the Southern branch of the All-sky BRIght, Complete Quasar Survey (AllBRICQS) at declinations $\text{Dec} < +20^\circ$ and Galactic latitudes $|b| > 10^\circ$. They select point-like sources from the Gaia satellite that show zero parallax or proper motion (filtering out nearby stars) and combine this with mid-infrared photometry from WISE to pick out the signature red thermal emission of hot dusty tori around quasars, following up candidates spectroscopically with the ANU 2.3m telescope. This provides a pure, flux-complete ($G_{\rm RP} < 16$) sample of the brightest Southern quasars, offering prime targets for high-resolution interferometry (like VLTI/GRAVITY+), intergalactic medium absorption studies, and cosmological reference frames.

papers.title: Spiralling into Dark Energy: Axio-Dilaton Attractors in Light of Current Data
papers.authors: Mario Ramos-Hamud
papers.abstract: In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-\xi\phi_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $\omega_\phi=(\lambda-2\xi)/(\lambda+2\xi)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $\xi\gg\lambda$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $\lambda\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}\xi\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $\Lambda$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539 .

conclusions: Non-geodesic late-time attractors yield a dark energy equation of state $w_\phi = (\lambda - 2\xi)/(\lambda + 2\xi)$, which approaches $-1$ without ever crossing into the phantom regime ($w_\phi < -1$) provided the kinetic coupling dominates the potential slope ($\xi \gg \lambda$).

Adding a linear polynomial prefactor ($n=1$) leaves the late-time attractors unchanged, while a quadratic Albrecht–Skordis correction ($n=2$) introduces a stable de Sitter minimum ($w_\phi = -1$) when $A\lambda^2 < 1$.

Combining DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon SNe, and Planck distance priors constrains $\lambda \gtrsim 7\text{--}9$ and $\log_{10}\xi \gtrsim 2.5$ (95% CL), driven by early dark energy bounds (which prevent $\lambda$ from being too small) and the need for late-time acceleration ($\xi \gg \lambda$).

The axio-dilaton models improve the fit over $\Lambda$CDM by $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm min} \approx -4$ to $-6$ for DESI DR2 BAO alone and $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm min} \approx -1.2$ for the full dataset combination, though the polynomial correction order $n$ remains unconstrained.

papers.title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy
papers.authors: Rashmikanta Mantry, Kazuyuki Furuuchi
papers.abstract: We explore effective field theory (EFT) realizations of the dark dimension (DD) scenario in which the size of the DD is determined by the competition between a 5D quintessence potential and the Casimir energy. When only contributions from massless fields are considered, the Casimir energy does not have a typical energy scale, and the 4D dark energy (DE) scale is set by the height of the 5D quintessence potential. The simple 5D model we first study has an attractive feature that the size of the DD is related to the 4D vacuum energy (VE), as outlined above. However, it turns out that the 4D VE thus obtained cannot work as the 4D DE in the standard cosmological setting. One of the discrepancies between the VE and the DE manifests in the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's gravitational constant. This leads us to explore a 5D model in which the 4D Einstein-Hilbert (EH) action is dominantly induced by quantum effects, leaving the radion dependence of the 4D Newton's constant subdominant. This model leads to an attractive cosmological model, realizing the mechanism explained in the beginning. We also explore a 6D model with the total internal volume fixed, to make the 4D Newton's constant independent of the radion. We first study a scenario in which the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions are of the same order. In this scenario, the physical origin of the size of the DD is left to its UV completion. Next, we turn to a scenario in which there is a large hierarchy between the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions. In this scenario, the energy scale of the 5D quintessence potential turns out to be much higher than the energy scale of the 4D DE as inferred from the cosmological observations, so we need to subtract a constant term in 4D to tune the 4D DE. This prevents us from obtaining the scaling relation for the DE expected in the dSDC.

conclusions: A minimal 5D setup balancing a quintessence potential against massless Casimir energy naturally links the extra dimension size $R$ to the 4D vacuum energy scale ($\rho_{\rm VE} \sim R^{-4}$), but fails cosmologically because the radion-dependent 4D gravitational constant modifies the Einstein frame potential and prevents accelerated expansion.

A viable 5D cosmological model is achieved if the 4D Einstein-Hilbert action is dominantly induced on a brane by quantum effects (analogous to DGP gravity in the small-extra-dimension regime), suppressing the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's constant $G_N$.

Extending the setup to 6D with a fixed total internal volume eliminates the variation of $G_N$; if the 5th and 6th dimensions have comparable sizes, the dark dimension scaling works phenomenologically, though fixing the total volume requires ultraviolet physics.

In a 6D scenario with a large hierarchy between the two extra dimensions, the 5D quintessence scale must be much higher than the observed dark energy density, requiring a 4D constant subtraction (fine-tuning) and spoiling the predicted Swampland scaling between dark energy and the extra dimension size.

They show that a naive 5D setup fails to produce viable 4D cosmic acceleration because the 4D Newton's constant depends on the radion, which distorts the effective dark energy potential upon converting to the 4D Einstein frame. To solve this, they construct two alternative frameworks that suppress the radion's coupling to 4D gravity—a 5D model with quantum-induced brane gravity and a 6D fixed-volume model—Clarifying which extra-dimensional setups can naturally link the dark energy scale to extra-dimensional geometry without fine-tuning.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Three-Dimensional Stellar Mass Profiles of Massive Galaxy Clusters
papers.authors: Jong-In Park, Jubee Sohn, I-Non Chiu
papers.abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional (3D) stellar mass profiles of galaxy clusters using simulations and observations. We develop the Projection-to-Enclosed Estimator by Layers (PEEL) model, which geometrically reconstructs the 3D stellar mass profile from the projected stellar mass profile under the assumption of spherical symmetry. Starting from the outermost annulus, the PEEL model subtracts the contributions of the outer shells from the projected mass in each inner annulus. Using 205 halos from the TNG-Cluster simulation, we show that the reconstructed profile (hereafter the PEEL profile) recovers the true 3D stellar mass profile without systematic bias. We also examine potential systematic effects, including the use of subhalos versus stellar particles, the choice of cluster center, and the 3D shape of the halo. We then apply the PEEL model to a stacked sample of nine massive clusters from the MAssive Cluster survey with Hectospec (MACH). The observed PEEL profile is much flatter than the simulated 3D profile, indicating that the simulated clusters have a more centrally concentrated stellar mass distribution, mainly because of an excess of extremely massive galaxies in their cores. Combining the PEEL profile with the total mass profile from the caustic technique, we derive the stellar mass fraction profile of the observed clusters. The stellar mass fraction remains nearly constant at $0.009 \pm 0.002$ within $R_{200}$, consistent with previous observations and with the simulated clusters. The PEEL model provides a practical tool for measuring the 3D stellar mass profiles of large cluster samples from future wide-field spectroscopic surveys.

conclusions: The PEEL model reconstructs 3D stellar mass profiles of stacked TNG-Cluster halos without systematic bias; for a 9-cluster stack matched to the MACH survey, the radially averaged offset is $-0.04$ dex, with a $1\sigma$ scatter ranging from $\sim 0.01$ dex in the core ($R < 0.2\,R_{200}$) to $\sim 0.4$ dex in the outskirts.

Systematic tests show that assigning stellar mass to individual particles rather than subhalo centers changes the profile by at most $\sim 40\%$ (reducing core mass by $\sim 19\%$), while cluster miscentering below the bin width ($0.2\,R_{200}$) has negligible impact on the deprojection.

TNG-Cluster halos exhibit a much steeper 3D stellar mass profile than the observed MACH clusters: simulations overpredict stellar mass within $0.2\,R_{200}$ by a factor of $\sim 5\text{--}6$ (driven by overly massive central galaxies above $10^{11}\,M_\odot$) and underpredict it beyond $1.5\,R_{200}$ by a factor of $\sim 2\text{--}4$ (due to a deficit of satellite galaxies).

Combining the deprojected stellar mass with dynamical caustic total masses yields an almost flat observed 3D stellar mass fraction profile of $f_\star(R) = 0.009 \pm 0.002$ within $R_{200}$ ($0.0076 \pm 0.0016$ within $R_{500}$), which matches TNG-Cluster between $0.2\,R_{200}$ and $R_{200}$ ($0.009 \pm 0.001$) but highlights a $4\times$ excess of stellar mass in the simulated cores.
ai.summary: Measuring how stellar mass is distributed in three dimensions within galaxy clusters tests how efficiently baryons cool and form stars during halo assembly, yet observations only capture 2D projections along the line of sight. To overcome this, the authors introduce the Projection-to-Enclosed Estimator by Layers (PEEL), an analytic geometric deprojection method that peels away outer spherical shells layer by layer to reconstruct the 3D stellar mass profile from 2D concentric annuli under spherical symmetry. They validate PEEL on 205 massive cluster halos from the hydrodynamical zoom-in simulation TNG-Cluster and apply it to a stacked sample of nine massive local clusters ($0.07 < z < 0.11$) from the deep spectroscopic MACH survey, combining the stellar profiles with dynamical total mass profiles derived from the caustic technique (which estimates mass from the escape velocity boundary in redshift space). While the integrated stellar mass fraction within $R_{200}$ agrees well between data and simulations, comparing the radial 3D profiles exposes a significant discrepancy in how current galaxy formation feedback models distribute stars between the cluster core and outskirts.

papers.title: ZTF-SEDm Type Ia supernova sample for Twins Embedding spectrophotometric standardization
papers.authors: C. Ganot, Y. Copin, M. Rigault, G. Dimitriadis, A. Goobar, K. Maguire, J. Nordin, M. Smith, G. Aldering, C. Barjou-Delayre, M. Betoule, J. S. Bloom, U. Burgaz, L. Galbany, M. Ginolin, M. Graham, D. Hale, J. Johansson, M.M. Kasliwal, Y.-L. Kim, F.J. Masci, T.E. Müller-Bravo, S. Perlmutter, B. Popovic, J.N. Purdum, B. Rusholme, J. Sollerman, J.H. Terwel, A. Townsend
papers.abstract: This paper has two aims: the first aim is to build a large homogeneous spectrophotometric sample of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), using 3069 spectra from the second data release of the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF DR2). Using this sample we reproduce, as the second objective of the paper, the Twins Embedding (TE) spectrophotometric standardization method, which led to an exceptionally low value of 0.073 mag for the intrinsic scatter. We improved the flux-calibration accuracy of the SEDm SN Ia spectrum sample using the ZTF photometric data, which are calibrated at the percent level. We then applied the three steps of the TE parameterization to a subset of 783 ZTF SN spectra near maximum light, and analyse the resulting standardization methods. The precision of the phase-correction model, which is the first step of the TE, is estimated at 0.01 mag in g band, using ZTF data. Despite the challenge posed by the ZTF spectrum-extraction pipeline, we applied a first standardization in color based on the second step of the TE, called Read Between The Lines (RBTL). When considering the scatter due to redshift error and flux calibration error, we estimated a 0.129 mag Hubble residual scatter for this ZTF sample as an upper limit. As expected from the low spectral quality, the final TE standardization based on three nonlinear parameters did not improve the overall dispersion. We release 1897 flux calibrated spectra of 1607 SNe Ia with an estimated photometric accuracy of 0.07 mag. We further demonstrate the ability to apply a spectrophotometric standardization with limited quality spectra. The RBTL standardisation is more efficient than that of SALT with one less parameter, and the resulting host steps are consistent with zero, making it less prone to astrophysical bias. For future spectroscopic surveys, a better spectral quality would enable the full TE standardization to be computed. (Abridged)

papers.title: Diffusive dark fluids with Planck-2018 and DESI BAO DR2 Measurements
papers.authors: Shambel Sahlu, Amare Abebe
papers.abstract: In this paper, we constrain the diffusive dark fluid cosmological model, wherein energy is transferred between the two dark components through a diffusion process. We extended the work in Ref. \cite{sahlu2026observational} by employing Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data from the Planck 2018 measurements in combination with Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 (2024). From the results, we found that the discrepancies in \(H_0\) measurements are \(1.90\sigma\) and \(1.72\sigma\) between the Planck 2018 value \((H_0 = 67.4\pm0.5\ \mathrm{km,s^{-1},Mpc^{-1}})\) and our diffusive model values, \(H_0 = 67.27^{+0.54}_{-0.55}\;,\) and \(68.35^{+0.31}_{-0.29} \), respectively. We also observe that the effects of the interaction on cosmic evolution and structure formation; we emphasize this by computing the scale-dependent density contrast and the matter power spectrum, compared with the $\Lambda$CDM model.

papers.title: Symmetry-Protected Momentum Exchange between Dark Matter and Dark Energy
papers.authors: Mohid Farhan
papers.abstract: We present a particle physics motivated realization of interacting dark energy in which a radiatively stable dark energy sector couples to weakly interacting massive particle dark matter through pure momentum exchange. The dark energy field arises as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson from a complex scalar singlet charged under a softly broken global $U(1)_S$, while dark matter is identified with an inert scalar doublet stabilized by a discrete $Z_4$ symmetry. This symmetry structure allows renormalizable dark matter-dark energy portal operators; however, requiring the dark energy field to emerge as a radiatively stable pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson necessitates their absence, leaving derivative interactions as the leading coupling. As a result, energy transfer between the dark sectors is absent at the background level, while momentum exchange modifies the evolution of cosmological perturbations. We implement the resulting interacting dark energy model self-consistently in the Boltzmann code CLASS and study its impact on the growth of structure. We find that, despite sizeable momentum exchange, the suppression of the clustering amplitude $\sigma_8$ saturates above the level required to fully resolve current low-redshift tensions. Our results demonstrate that symmetry-protected, momentum-exchange-only dark sector interactions possess an intrinsic limit on structure suppression, providing a theoretically controlled benchmark for interacting dark energy scenarios.

papers.title: Calibration-Induced Systematics in SALT3 Training and Their Impact on Dark Energy Constraints from Stage IV Supernova Surveys
papers.authors: Kene Anumba, David O. Jones, Richard Kessler, Daniel Scolnic, W. D'Arcy Kenworthy, Rebecca C. Chen, Bastien Carreres, Maria Vincenzi, Erik R. Peterson, Maria Acevedo, Ben Rose, Dillon Brout, Jillian Paulin, Rujuta A. Purohit, Rebekah Hounsell, The Roman Supernova Cosmology Project Infrastructure Team
papers.abstract: In the coming years, the Vera Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (Rubin-LSST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's (Roman) High Latitude Time Domain Survey (HLTDS) are expected to discover more than a million Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), several orders of magnitude more than current samples and with a tighter control on systematic uncertainties. One of the largest systematic uncertainties in cosmological analyses with SNe Ia is the accuracy of the spectrophotometric model for SNe Ia time series data, which depends on the photometric calibration of the surveys. To quantify the impact of this uncertainty, we analyze simulated Rubin-LSST and HLTDS data, perturb the photometric zero-points and filter mean wavelengths, and propagate these systematics to spectral model recovery, estimated distances, and dark energy Figure of merit (FoM) based on the $w_0 w_a$CDM model. Zero-point shifts of 5 mmag and filter mean wavelength shifts of 5 angstrom lead to a $\sim 50\%$ decrease in the FoM relative to a statistical-only case when calibration uncertainties are propagated only through light-curve fitting. The same calibration shifts applied only during model training produce a smaller $\sim 13\%$ degradation. Contrary to previous analyses, calibration uncertainties in light-curve fitting dominate over those from model training. Their effect during light-curve fitting varies smoothly with redshift and is nearly degenerate with cosmology, preventing mitigation through self-calibration. Finally, we show that the FoM dependence on the size of the calibration uncertainties (in the range of expected sizes) is roughly linear.

papers.title: Cosmic-web Environmental Impacts on the Halo Substructure Boosts to Dark Matter Annihilation Signals
papers.authors: Feven Markos Hunde, Wojciech A. Hellwing, Maciej Bilicki
papers.abstract: The annihilation of dark matter (DM) particles is expected to produce Standard Model particles, providing a potential indirect signature of DM. The clumpy substructure of DM haloes amplifies the expected annihilation signal, an effect commonly quantified by the subhalo boost factor. Standard semi-analytic models usually treat this boost as a universal function of host-halo mass, neglecting systematic variations induced by the large-scale environment. In this work, we extend this framework by incorporating the influence of the cosmic web on subhalo populations. Using simulation-calibrated, environment-dependent ratios for host-halo concentrations, the subhalo mass function, and internal-structure proxies of subhalos based on the $V_{\max}$--$R_{\max}$ relation, we compute environment-conditioned boost predictions for haloes residing in filaments, walls, and voids. Our main result is the boost factor at fixed host-halo mass, expressed relative to the cosmic-mean prediction, $B(M,\mathrm{env})/B_{\mathrm{CM}}(M)$. We find a clear environmental modulation: in the fiducial distance-dependent model, filament haloes show a mass-dependent transition from a $\sim 15\%$ suppression at the low-mass end to a modest enhancement of $\sim 12\%$ for massive hosts, wall haloes remain intermediate, while void haloes stay suppressed by roughly $30$--$33\%$ across the explored host-mass range. These results should be interpreted as deterministic model predictions obtained by propagating environment-dependent ingredient ratios through two standard semi-analytic boost frameworks. We provide an environment-aware prescription for subhalo boosts, together with modular environmental corrections that may also be useful in indirect-detection forecasts, strong-lensing mass modeling, and related halo-population applications.

papers.title: Constraints on Horndeski gravity with phantom crossing
papers.authors: Krishna Naidoo, James Hallam, Tessa Baker, Sergi Sirera
papers.abstract: Gravity models in which the dark energy equation of state crosses $w=-1$, also known as the phantom divide, have received extensive interest due to recent analyses favouring this behaviour. We introduce a new subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor models capable of generating phantom crossing, whilst remaining minimally coupled to matter: the Asymptotic Cubic Galileon (ACG) models. We show that ACG models can jointly fit the expansion history inferred from observations of the Planck cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, and distance-ladder supernovae measurements from the Dark Energy Survey. We then demonstrate that requiring a positive galaxy-ISW cross-correlation, together with physically viable screening behaviour, substantially restricts the viable ACG parameter space. Model comparison metrics, including $\chi^{2}$ and Bayesian evidence, favour both ACG and $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM models over $\Lambda$CDM, with ACG providing a fit of comparable quality to $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM. Crucially, ACG models ground the observationally preferred $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM behaviour in a robust Lagrangian formulation. This enables interpretation beyond mere phenomenological fits, and motivates further tests of these models on nonlinear scales.

papers.title: CHEX-MATE: AMALGAM weak-lensing analysis of 41 Planck Sunyaev-Zel'dovich-selected galaxy clusters
papers.authors: Keiichi Umetsu, Raphael Gavazzi, Mauro Sereno, Nobuhiro Okabe, Emmanuel Bertin, Gianluca Castignani, Stefano Ettori, Fabio Gastaldello, Carlo Giocoli, Scott T. Kay, Junhan Kim, Maggie Lieu, Lorenzo Lovisari, Ben J. Maughan, Mario Nonino, Lorenzo Pizzuti, Etienne Pointecouteau, Gabriel W. Pratt, Mario Radovich, Elena Rasia, Mariachiara Rossetti, Harshda Saxena, Jack Sayers
papers.abstract: We present a weak-lensing shear analysis of 41 Planck SZ-selected galaxy clusters at $0.11\le z\le 0.55$ from the CHEX-MATE sample, using wide-field Subaru/Suprime-Cam and CFHT/MegaPrime imaging from the AMALGAM project. We detect the azimuthally averaged weak-lensing signal around the X-ray peak of each cluster, achieving a median S/N of 6.5 per cluster. The $45^\circ$-rotated component has a median S/N of -0.1 and ranges from -1.8 to +1.8, consistent with zero. We model the excess surface mass density profile of each cluster with an NFW profile to infer weak-lensing mass and concentration constraints. The total systematic uncertainty in the weak-lensing mass calibration is assessed to be $8\%$. Using a hierarchical Bayesian framework, we then derive weak-lensing-calibrated scaling relations for the halo concentration, $c_{200}$, as a function of $M_{200}$ and redshift, and for the Planck SZ mass proxy, $M_{SZ}$, as a function of $M_{500}$ and redshift, while accounting for sample selection effects, weak-lensing modelling biases, and residual calibration uncertainty. At $M_{200}=10^{15}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, we find $c_{200}=3.53\pm0.71$ with an intrinsic scatter of $0.22\pm0.04$ dex. The inferred normalisation and scatter are consistent with recent $\Lambda$CDM predictions for massive haloes, with no significant mass or redshift dependence over the probed range. For the Planck mass proxy, our baseline regression yields $M_{SZ}/M_{500}=0.83\pm0.09$ at $M_{500}=7\times10^{14}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.10\pm0.02$ dex. A restricted model with fixed unit mass slope and no redshift evolution gives $1-b=0.72\pm0.11$. We also provide weak-lensing-calibrated posterior estimates of $M_{500}$ for the sample based on the baseline $M_{SZ}$--$M_{500}$--$z$ relation. These results provide an initial weak-lensing mass calibration for CHEX-MATE multi-probe cluster studies.

papers.title: Strong Lensing Tomography: Double and pseudo multi-source plane strong gravitational lensing to constrain dark energy
papers.authors: Paras Sharma, Simon Birrer, Narayan Khadka, Timo Anguita, Adam Bolton, Sydney Erickson, Phil Holloway, Tian Li, Phil Marshall, Dieu D. Nguyen, Graham P. Smith, Crescenzo Tortora, Bryce Wedig, the Strong Lensing Science Collaboration, the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration
papers.abstract: Tomographic measurements of gravitational lensing with different lens and source redshift distributions contain crucial information about the universe's relative expansion rate, and hence dark energy. While this technique is well-established in weak lensing, its application to strong lensing has traditionally focused on Double Source Plane Lenses (DSPLs). However, DSPLs are exceedingly rare and fundamentally limited by the Mass-Sheet Degeneracy (MSD), a systematic uncertainty underexplored in previous literature. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Pseudo Double-Source Plane Lenses (PDSPLs): pairs of independent single-source plane lenses with self-similar deflectors. This generalizes the DSPL formalism to the $\sim 10^5$ galaxy-galaxy lenses expected from LSST, Euclid, and Roman. Unlike true DSPLs, PDSPLs are free from the intermediate source mass problem by construction, eliminating the associated secondary MSD and the need for multi-plane ray tracing. We incorporate the deflector MSD into a hierarchical population model to forecast dark energy constraints in Flat $w_0w_a$CDM, showing that MSD severely degrades constraints from small DSPL samples and motivates our PDSPL statistical approach. Assuming unbiased Gaussian photo-z errors of $\sigma_z/(1+z)=0.03$, the mock LSST Y10 photometric sample yields $\sigma(w_0)\sim0.45$, constraining the population-mean MSD parameter and deflector power-law slope to $\sim2\%$. A prior $\Omega_m\sim\mathcal{N}(0.3,0.05)$, representing combination with external cosmological probes such as CMB, BAO, or SNe Ia, improves this to $\sigma(w_0)\sim0.29$, comparable to Stage III weak lensing. The statistical advantage over smaller spectroscopic subsets (e.g., 4MOST) assumes unbiased photo-zs. Real-data use requires spectroscopic photo-z calibration and validation of how paired deflectors' mass-profile differences affect Einstein-radius ratios.

papers.title: Probing Graviton Mass with MeerKAT PTA and SKA-PTA Forecasts
papers.authors: Zhi-Chao Zhao, Sai Wang
papers.abstract: In this study, we derive constraints on the graviton mass using the 4.5-year data release from the MeerKAT Pulsar Timing Array (MPTA) and provide forecasts for the upcoming Square Kilometre Array PTA (SKA-PTA). By modeling the modified dispersion relation and the corresponding tensor correlation function for massive gravitons, we perform Bayesian inference on the angular-correlation measurements under three noise configurations. Our 90\% credible upper limits on the graviton mass span $m_g < (2.10$-$2.58) \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$. Including monopolar and dipolar contributions does not significantly alter these bounds, confirming that the constraints are driven by the quadrupolar tensor correlation. All results remain fully consistent with general relativity. For SKA-PTA, we forecast sensitivities down to $m_g \sim 10^{-24}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 10-year observing baseline and $m_g \sim 10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 50-year observing baseline, representing order-of-magnitude improvements over current limits. This work demonstrates the power of current and future PTA observations to test fundamental aspects of gravity in the nanohertz band.

papers.title: Axion Inflation: Perturbative control in the strong backreaction regime
papers.authors: Valerie Domcke, Alexandros Papageorgiou, Marco Peloso, Stefan Sandner
papers.abstract: We study the strong backreaction regime in axion inflation, in which the friction from Abelian gauge fields generated via the pseudo-scalar interaction $\frac{\beta}{4 M_p} \phi F {\tilde F}$ is comparable to Hubble friction. The non-linear dynamics associated with the gauge fields render this regime phenomenologically particularly interesting, but also notoriously difficult to study with perturbative methods. Quantifying the perturbative control through the direct impact on the spectral backreaction using (i) a first-order gradient-expansion formalism including axion gradients, and (ii) a one-loop in-in calculation, we discover an extended mild backreaction regime at large couplings $\beta$, with a relatively large, nearly constant particle production parameter $\xi$. In passing, we point out that CMB non-Gaussianity bounds impose a general upper limit on the product of axion gauge field coupling and Hubble parameter during inflation, $\beta H/M_p < 1.4\cdot 10^{-3}$, independently of the choice of the axion potential.

papers.title: Late-Time Emergence of Dark Energy and Its Interaction with Dark Matter
papers.authors: Sibo Zhang, Weiqiang Yang, Supriya Pan, Olga Mena, Eleonora Di Valentino, Subenoy Chakraborty
papers.abstract: We present an interacting scenario between dark energy (DE) and dark matter (DM), where DE has an emergent nature, that means, DE was absent in the early universe but it becomes effective only at late times. We consider two specific emergent DE models, one with no free parameters and the other featuring two parameters describing the speed and epoch of the transition. We constrain both scenarios using the cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements from the Planck 2018 release, baryon acoustic oscillations from DESI DR2, and three different compilations of Type Ia supernovae (PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, and Union3). Our analysis indicates that current cosmological probes are not able to tightly constrain the speed of the transition. For both scenarios, the posterior distribution of the interaction parameter is shifted away from zero at more than 95\% CL whenever the CMB data are combined with any of these additional probes, with the preferred direction corresponding to a transfer of energy from DE to DM. While CMB alone yields a high value of $H_0$, in agreement with local determinations, this effect is reduced when DESI is added and disappears once supernova data are included. In contrast, the clustering parameter $S_8$ is consistently shifted toward lower values in the combined datasets, and it is correlated with the preference for a negative interaction. However, according to the $\Delta \chi^2_{\rm min}$ and Bayesian evidence, none of the interacting models is favored over $\Lambda$CDM or $w_0w_a$CDM, indicating that the interaction does not rescue these emergent DE models. Our results therefore highlight the limitations of these scenarios in addressing current cosmological tensions, while pointing to the crucial role of future data in further assessing their viability.

papers.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
papers.authors: Oliver H. E. Philcox
papers.abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic and counterterm contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the VEGAS algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.20h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$, or $0.27h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.42h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for an emission line galaxy sample at $z=1.1$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $\sigma_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.authors: Martin Rosenlyst, Vinh Tran, Oliver Zier, Xuejian Shen, Mark Vogelsberger, Thejs Brinckmann, Mads T. Frandsen, Jesús Zavala, Frederik Holt Dihver Christensen, Mikkel Theiss Kristensen
papers.abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate these implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish agreement across numerical schemes, and reproduce published benchmarks. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

papers.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
papers.authors: Gert Hütsi
papers.abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.

papers.title: Environmental dependence of galaxy properties in the southern GAMA regions
papers.authors: Koti Joy, Unnikrishnan Sureshkumar, Anand Narayanan, Anna Durkalec, Sabine Bellstedt, Agnieszka Pollo, Matt Hilton
papers.abstract: Using data from the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey, we investigate how galaxy properties correlate with the local environment, focusing on its two southern regions (G02 and G23) that have not previously been examined in this context. We employ two-point and marked correlation functions to quantify the environmental dependence of galaxy color, stellar mass, luminosity across the $u$, $g$, $r$, $J$, and $K$ bands, as well as star formation rate (SFR) and specific star formation rate (sSFR). Our results show that $u-r$ and $g-r$ colors are most strongly correlated with local overdensity, followed by stellar mass. The SFR and sSFR exhibit a clear inverse relationship with environmental density, consistent with the trend observed for $u$-band luminosity, which traces young stellar populations. The galaxies brighter in the $g$, $J$, and $K$ bands preferentially inhabit denser regions. We interpret the environmental dependence of color using Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) modeling. The HOD modeling indicates that red galaxies trace dense environments more strongly than blue galaxies, exhibiting significantly higher satellite fractions and occupying more massive halos. We demonstrate that both redshift and stellar mass incompleteness systematically affect clustering measurements, generally enhancing the observed environmental dependence. Comparing our measurements from the southern regions with those from the equatorial GAMA regions, we find that the overall environmental trends remain consistent. The measured correlations provide key constraints for models of galaxy assembly across mass and environment, while environmental trends in color and near-infrared luminosity trace stellar mass growth and quenching with redshift.

Ball, G. Ballardin, S. W. Ballmer, S. Banagiri, B. Banerjee, D. Bankar, T. M. Baptiste, P. Baral, M. Baratti, J. C. Barayoga, B. C. Barish, D. Barker
papers.abstract: We search for gravitational-wave background signals produced by various early Universe processes in the Advanced LIGO O4a dataset, combined with the data from the earlier O1, O2, and O3 (LIGO-Virgo) runs. The absence of detectable signals enables powerful constraints on fundamental physics. We derive gravitational-wave background energy density upper limits from the O1-O4a data to constrain parameters associated with various possible processes in the early Universe: first-order phase transitions, cosmic strings, domain walls, stiff equation of state, axion inflation, second-order scalar perturbations, primordial black hole binaries, and parity violation. In our analyses, the presence of an astrophysical background produced by compact (black hole and neutron star) binary coalescences throughout the Universe is also considered. We address the implications for various cosmological and high energy physics models based on the obtained parameter constraints. We conclude that LIGO-Virgo data already yield significant constraints on numerous early Universe scenarios.

papers.title: p-Wave Dominant Majorana Dark Matter and Its Self-Interactions in a Gauged $U(1)_{L_μ- L_τ}$ Model
papers.authors: Kwei-Chou Yang
papers.abstract: We propose a model of $p$-wave dominant Majorana dark matter (DM) featuring a macroscopic mass gap in a gauged $U(1)_{L_\mu - L_\tau}$ extension of the Standard Model. Spontaneous symmetry breaking generates a dominant Majorana mass via a strong Yukawa coupling, splitting the dark fermion into two distinct states. The lighter state ($\chi_-$) is the DM candidate, with an allowed mass of $\sim 10$ GeV to several hundred GeV. Crucially, within the $10 \sim 75$ GeV mass range and a scalar mediator at the tens of MeV scale, this strong coupling dictates the thermal relic abundance and induces significant elastic self-interactions. These self-interactions naturally resolve small-scale structure anomalies, such as the core-cusp problem, while satisfying massive cluster constraints. Furthermore, we place stringent joint constraints on the scalar mass and the Higgs mixing angle $\alpha$ using the latest LZ 2025 direct detection data. The model's gauge boson $Z^\prime$ maintains early-Universe thermal equilibrium and accommodates the muon anomalous magnetic moment $(g-2)_\mu$, remaining consistent with updated cosmological and experimental bounds.

papers.title: What does it take to have $N_{\rm eff} < 3$ at CMB times?
papers.authors: Miguel Escudero, Maksym Ovchynnikov, Neal Weiner
papers.abstract: The vast majority of extensions of the Standard Model affecting the number of effective relativistic neutrino species ($N_{\rm eff}$) do so additively, namely, they enhance this quantity with some light state contributing to dark radiation. In this work, we consider precisely the opposite case: new physics scenarios that can lead to $N_{\rm eff} < 3$ that are consistent with all known cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory data. We are motivated by three main reasons: 1) a recent measurement from ACT and SPT in combination with Planck that leads to $N_{\rm eff} = 2.81\pm0.12$, 2) by a new and powerful measurement of the primordial helium abundance, which anchors $N_{\rm eff}$ to be very close to the Standard Model value one second after the Big Bang, 3) by the deployment of the Simons Observatory which will provide precise tests of the radiation content in the Universe and which may detect with a high significance cosmologies with $N_{\rm eff}<3$. We survey the main theoretical possibilities and find that only a few simple scenarios can consistently give $N_{\rm eff}=2.81\pm0.12$. One class consists of thermal electrophilic relics with masses $m\sim 8\!-\!13\,{\rm MeV}$. Another consists of out-of-equilibrium particles decaying to $e^+e^-$ or $\gamma\gamma$, with a rather particular lifetime $0.05\,{\rm s}\lesssim \tau \lesssim 3\,{\rm min}$, mass $250\,{\rm MeV}\lesssim m \lesssim 600\,{\rm MeV}$, and abundance $\rho/\rho_\gamma\sim 0.1$ at decay. Thermal electrophilic particles are especially interesting because they can account for the dark matter in the Universe and can be tested in experiments such as SENSEI, DAMIC-M, and Oscura, and their portals to the visible sector at experiments such as NA64 and LDMX. We conclude that if the Simons Observatory confirms that $N_{\rm eff} \simeq 2.8$, it will point to very specific extensions of the Standard Model.

papers.title: Quasi-linear theory of fast flavor instabilities in homogeneous environments
papers.authors: Damiano F. G. Fiorillo, Georg G. Raffelt
papers.abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves, for the first time, as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasi-linear theory (QLT), including backreaction on the neutrino distribution and nonresonant neutrino--flavomon interactions, while neglecting wave--wave processes. In a homogeneous, axisymmetric model, the saturated neutrino and flavomon distributions agree closely with periodic-box solutions of the original quantum kinetic equation. These results support the use of QLT, well established in plasma physics, to bypass nonlinear small-scale effects that challenge direct simulations.

papers.title: Modified Cosmology from Mass-to-Horizon Relation: Observational Bounds
papers.authors: Pranav Prasanthan, Hussain Gohar, Vincenzo Salzano
papers.abstract: We constrain the class of modified cosmologies derived in Paper I [1] from a generalized mass-to-horizon relation (MHR) that enforces thermodynamic consistency between the Cai-Kim horizon temperature and generalized horizon entropies. The modified Friedmann equations depend on an entropy exponent $m$, an MHR coupling parameter $\gamma$, and an entanglement-correction amplitude $f_B$, with standard $\Lambda$CDM recovered in the appropriate limit. Using Pantheon$+$/SH0ES Type~Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, we constrain eight physically motivated sub-cases via Markov chain Monte Carlo and compare models through the Bayesian log-evidence. The entropy exponent is tightly bounded, $|m-1|\lesssim O(10^{-4})$ when the MHR coupling is fixed ($\gamma=1$), relaxing to $O(10^{-3})$ along the $m$-$\gamma$ degeneracy, excluding any macroscopically significant departure from standard horizon thermodynamics. Freeing the MHR coupling parameter or the entanglement amplitude raises the inferred Hubble constant to $h\simeq0.70$-$0.71$, reducing the CMB-SH0ES tension from ${\sim}4\sigma$ to ${\sim}1.2$-$2.6\sigma$, but no scenario fully resolves it within a flat universe. The Bayesian log-evidence nevertheless disfavors every extension relative to $\Lambda$CDM in all dataset combinations ($-16\lesssim\Delta\ln Z \lesssim-1$): the improved fits obtained when the SH0ES calibration is included reflect an absorption of the Hubble tension by the additional parameters rather than genuine evidence for modified horizon entropy.

papers.title: Resolving Galactic and Cluster Dynamics Without Dark Matter: Tsallis Entropy as the Unique Foundation of Emergent Gravity
papers.authors: S. Shamari, A. Sheykhi
papers.abstract: While modified entropy models-such as Barrow, Tsallis, Kaniadakis,Power-law, Logarithmic, and Rényi entropies-have been widely explored in cosmological contexts, their implications on galactic scales remain largely untested. These generalizations of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy encode quantum gravitational, nonextensive, or fractal spacetime effects and can alter the gravitational entropy-area relation. In this paper, we demonstrate that the entropic force framework, when applied to galactic rotation curves and the baryonic mass of galaxy clusters, uniquely selects Tsallis entropy as the specific generalized entropy formulation. We then extend this Tsallis modified gravity to globular clusters to complete the structural hierarchy from galaxies to galaxy clusters to globular clusters and to investigate its behavior as a function of system scale. We will show that the nonextensive parameter exhibits no correlation with any of the macroscopic quantities characterizing gravitational systems, such as mass, radius, temperature, or density. Furthermore, it has previously been shown that entropy is not well-defined within the standard thermodynamic approach to gravity. The adoption of nonextensive statistics provides a foundation for entanglement, thereby enabling a consistent definition of entanglement entropy. We predict the existence of galaxy clusters with $\delta = 1$ (i.e., clusters whose dynamics require no dark matter) analogous to $\delta = 1$ systems already observed at galactic and globular cluster scales. This prediction provides a unique observational test to discriminate Tsallis gravity from $\Lambda$CDM and MOND. Therefore, for the entropic gravity paradigm to be consistent with observational data across all scales-from globular clusters to galaxies to galaxy clusters-it is inevitably required to be built upon \textit{Tsallis} entropy.

papers.title: Axion-driven spontaneous leptogenesis, precisely
papers.authors: Konstantin Kuckenberg, Martin A. Mojahed, Kai Schmitz, Hidenaga Watanabe
papers.abstract: We revisit a minimal scenario for spontaneous leptogenesis where the asymmetry generation is driven by a heavy axion-like field evolving via standard misalignment. We focus on the simplest framework in which lepton number violation originates from the dimension-five Weinberg operator and contributions from standard thermal leptogenesis become negligible. The asymmetry is computed by solving a set of transport equations, which incorporate fully flavor-dependent interaction rates for the Weinberg operator that are presented here for the first time. We also derive a simple algebraic master formula for the generated $B\!-\!L$ asymmetry, valid for arbitrary axion velocities and classically shift-symmetric couplings to the Standard Model, that reproduces the $B\!-\!L$-production dynamics of the full set of transport equations in controlled parameter regions. Along the way, we quantify the importance of low-scale neutrino masses and the two mass orderings on the final prediction for the generated asymmetry. Finally, we assess the cosmological viability of different axion couplings by accounting for entropy dilution from late-time axion decays and imposing constraints from baryonic isocurvature perturbations. We demonstrate that explaining the baryon asymmetry via standard Majoron misalignment is under severe tension due to dilution from late-time decays. In contrast, axions coupled to strong or weak sphalerons can successfully produce the observed asymmetry for decay constants near the energy scale of grand unification and axion oscillation temperatures $T_{\text{osc}} \gtrsim 10^{11\cdots12}$ GeV, provided a cosmological history featuring high-scale inflation and efficient reheating.

papers.title: Primordial Black Hole Seeds for Little Red Dots in $f(R)$ Gravity
papers.authors: Saeed Fakhry
papers.abstract: The little red dots (LRDs) discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope host black holes of up to $10^{9}\,M_{\odot}$ within the first billion years, posing a challenge to conventional seeding scenarios. We investigate whether such seeds can form in dense clusters of primordial black holes (PBHs), in which the central object grows by gravitational capture of the surrounding PBHs while accreting gas, within Hu-Sawicki $f(R)$ gravity, where the scalar field acts on the matter surrounding the PBHs. For the adopted cluster configuration, our results show that accretion and mergers reinforce one another: for time-averaged Eddington ratios $\lambda_{\rm Edd}\gtrsim0.3$, the seed consumes its cluster by $z\simeq5.5$-$7.3$ and subsequently grows into the LRD mass range. Calibrated on the observed black-hole mass function, the model reproduces the abundance of LRDs near the peak of their population without further adjustment, while it underpredicts the abundance at $z\simeq7.5$ and overpredicts it at $z\simeq2$. Our findings indicate that the earliest seeds may accrete about twice as efficiently as later ones, and that the finite cluster reservoir can imprint a lower edge on the mass function near the cluster mass. Within the adopted screening and halo-growth prescriptions, the scalar field enhances the abundance of active seeds by up to $\sim 13\%$ at lower redshifts and by $\sim 7\%$ at $z \simeq 7.5$ for the strongest model considered, modestly moving the high-redshift prediction towards the data at fixed normalization. Also, the remnant spins can further discriminate between feeding modes.

papers.title: Hybrid Partial Dressing: Correct Effective Potentials at All Temperatures
papers.authors: Raphaël Berthiaume, David Curtin, Michael Luke, Andrija Rasovic, Jyotirmoy Roy
papers.abstract: We develop Hybrid Partial Dressing (HPD), a simple diagrammatic resummation scheme for finite-temperature effective potentials in scalar field theory which is valid at all temperatures. HPD improves on earlier resummation schemes such as Daisy Resummation and Partial Dressing by being two-loop exact at all temperatures and free of the overlapping momentum problem. Renormalization group improvement is straightforward to implement. We illustrate the scheme in multi-scalar theories with a spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, and compare it against existing approaches, showing in particular that it reproduces the two-loop Dimensional Reduction (DR) potential exactly in the high-temperature regime where DR applies, while remaining valid at all temperatures. This makes HPD suitable for the general study of strong first order phase transitions beyond the Standard Model, as we demonstrate through gravitational wave predictions from HPD and its RG-improved version, RGHPD.

papers.title: A scalar-extended ${\rm U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}}$ explanation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV excess
papers.authors: Dipankar Pradhan, Abhik Sarkar
papers.abstract: The recently observed dark matter (DM) nuclear recoil event at an energy of $248 \pm 23\,(\text{stat.}) \pm 23\,(\text{syst.})\,\text{keV}$ at the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, favoring an inelastic scattering interpretation, has motivated various beyond the Standard Model (BSM) scenarios aimed at explaining the observed excess. In particular, this provides an opportunity to probe models that naturally accommodate inelastic DM scattering. In this work, we explore one such possibility by extending the $\rm U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}}$ model with two complex scalar fields, $\Phi$ and $S$, carrying charges $-1$ and $+2$, respectively, under the $\rm U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}}$ gauge symmetry. These charge assignments allow a trilinear interaction between the two scalar fields, which is crucial for generating the DM mass splitting. Following the spontaneous breaking of the $\rm U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}}$ symmetry, with $S$ acquiring a vacuum expectation value and generating a mass for the BSM gauge boson $Z_{\mu\tau}$, the real and imaginary components of $\Phi$ acquire a mass splitting. This naturally gives rise to an inelastic DM scattering scenario that can accommodate the LZ excess. We perform a likelihood-based assessment of the sensitivity of the model parameters to the observed event while consistently accounting for other relevant phenomenological constraints. Finally, we discuss the prospects for probing the viable parameter space at future experiments.
